Plain floors change **what makes a pair*: Plain floors change **what makes a pair**, more of them the deeper you go - one in the Gate, two in the Living Dungeon, three in the Deep, and in the Abyss every plain floor after its first - and the crown says so before your first flip. On **Opposites** every pair is one picture in two **opposite elements** - ember with tide, moss with bone: one card of each pair wears its opposite on its back and its face, so a card’s partner wears the other colour. Each card is still its true element to everything it does: what it casts, what it pops, how it reacts. On **Element pairs** any two plain cards of **one element** are a pair, whatever the picture, and the backs keep their element hidden: remember the colours you turn. A marked card - a Wanderer, a mask, a Sleeper, an odd card - keeps its own partner, and the two cards left behind by an element match become a pair of their own. On **Triples** some pictures come in **threes**, and each card of a three wears three pips on its back. Turn two of a three and they wait face up: the **third** claims all three as one match; any other card is a miss, and all three turn back. Past the Gate a floor may take **Sequences**: threes whose cards wear one, two or three pips, their **place** in the three. Turn the one, then the two, then the three of one picture to claim them; a two before its one, or a three before its two, is a miss at once.
